title: Custodian-led recertification playback and signed evidence export pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: build a custodian-driven recertification workflow that can (1) run scheduled or on-demand periodic reviews, (2) produce a cryptographically signed evidence bundle suitable for auditors, and (3) provide a deterministic 'playback' engine that reconstructs tenant access state at any point in the retention window.

Why: current exports surface snapshots but auditors ask for reproducible timelines and provenance (who changed what, when, and why). A playback capability + signed bundles closes the gap for regulated customers and reduces manual evidence assembly.

Scope: backend pipeline to assemble SCIM snapshots, SSO assertion logs, RBAC role-change events, and justification metadata; signing service to produce tamper-evident bundles; an API to request on-demand exports; minimal console UI for custodians to run and annotate reviews; retention-aware export generation honoring tenant residency policies.

Non-goals: full open-source audit tool, interactive auditor UI beyond exports, migrating existing long-term retention store (we will read from current retention bucket).

Telemetry: track export generation latency, bundle size distribution, playback reconstruction time percentiles, and failure/error rates per-tenant.

Security: signed bundles use KMS-backed keys with key-rotation metadata included in the bundle manifest. All export endpoints require elevated audit scope and must pass rate-limiting and authorization checks.

Deliverables: API endpoints (POST /exports, GET /exports/:id), signed bundle spec (manifest + compressed data + signature), playback service CLI/API for deterministic state reconstruction, console flow for custodians, docs and acceptance tests.
acceptance_criteria: Signed evidence bundle includes manifest, SCIM snapshot(s), SSO/IdP assertion logs, RBAC role change events, and signer metadata
Export API can be requested synchronously for small tenants (<1000 users) and asynchronously for large tenants with job status updates
Playback API reconstructs tenant access at requested timestamp within retention window and verifies event causality
Bundles are signed with KMS-managed key; signature validation available to auditors via public key endpoint
Console has a custodian flow to run on-demand recertifications, add reviewer annotations, and trigger export generation
All exports respect tenant data residency and retention settings; attempts to export out-of-residency data are denied and logged
End-to-end tests and a sample auditor checklist are included in the PR
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with PM/Design/Infra. Agreed MVP scope: signed bundles + basic playback + console trigger.
2026-02-28: Spike results - reconstructing access state from event-log + SCIM deltas is feasible; baseline playback for 30-day retention tenants averages 2.1s per 1000 events.
2026-03-04: Design review - Design suggested adding reviewer annotation fields and export purpose enum to manifest.
2026-03-09: Security consult - KMS key rotation requirements documented; recommended including signature verification helper in auditor docs.
2026-03-12: Implementation - PR opened for export job scheduler and bundle generator (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12483).
comments: PM (Evelyn Chen): Please ensure the export manifest includes a clear mapping of SCIM resource IDs to user-visible identifiers (email, external_id). Auditors repeatedly ask for stable identifiers.
Design (Marco Ruiz): Console UX should default to 'preview mode' showing estimated bundle size and expected runtime before triggering a large export.
Infra (Priya Nair): Recommend a quarantine bucket for generated bundles with separate retention policy and access controls; will provide storage ARN template.
Eng (Diego Morales): We should reuse the existing event-aggregator microservice to assemble RBAC events to avoid duplicating ingestion logic.
QA (Samir Gupta): Add deterministic fixtures for playback acceptance tests; will propose 3 sample tenant scenarios (small, medium, large).
